$comment: U36 -- C67 10 uF/0603 becomes 22 uF/0805 (C45783), matching C66 at FPC1 and
C68 at FPC3. The land pattern was inherited from the EasyEDA import, not
chosen: C67 was the board's only 10 V part, and after DC-bias derating at
3.3 V it delivered nearer 5 uF against its siblings' ~17 uF. The footprint
swap itself is applied through pcbnew; this file is the copper that has to
move because of it.
Only ONE thing actually has to move. Going 0603 -> 0805 pushes the pads from
+/-0.700 to +/-1.000 and grows them to 1.410 x 1.350, so pad 2 (/GND) now
spans y 92.995..94.405 -- and the /GND stitching via sat at (140.350,94.300),
INSIDE that. Same net, so DRC would never complain; it would simply be a via
in a pad, and reflow would wick solder down the barrel.
The /+3V3 side needs nothing: its track already started at (140.350,92.000),
which the larger pad 1 (y 90.995..92.405) still covers.
The via cannot simply move south. The /I2C_SCL Inner1 diagonal runs
y = x - 44.900 overhead, and a 0.6 via needs its centre 0.7476 mm clear of it
in y, capping the via at y <= 94.702 -- while clearing the new pad needs
y > 94.705. Infeasible at x=140.350, by 3 um. Moving EAST opens it: the
diagonal climbs away as x grows, so at x=141.000 the clearance is 0.849
against the 0.5286 required, and the via still clears pad 2's corner by

steps.step: 1/1  move the /GND stitching via out from under the new 0805 pad
